input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: § 2.1 expressly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies, that Customer pays only for Services ordered under a signed Order Form, and that declining to place further orders is neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 7.1 (Vendor may not impose an unstated minimum-use charge) and § 12 (acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). There is no take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, no-downgrade-at-renewal, or volume cap on Customer usage: § 8.2 renewals are terminable on thirty days' notice by Customer with no quantity floor, and § 13 contains no usage caps. No redline required. (Separately noted, not under this rule: § 7.7 late-payment liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week is an unrelated payment-terms issue for the applicable rule.)
